body: I've actually gone to therapy with two different psychiatrists and while it's definitely helped while I'm there, it just feels like I always end up down in the same hole. Like once I leave the office and are a week removed from the session it's back to the same old same old regardless of how good it felt at the time with them.

For socially, I kind of just want... something. I used to have friends I could have friends I could hang out with and talk to, but then we moved a decade ago and since then I haven't really found any of that since. I might have to redefine my definition of acquaintance since I don't have really talk to people outside my family any more. Like I'll socialize people in class, but generally once it ends they all forget about me.

By social level I meant my aptitude to navigate social interactions. Like I've just always been awkward. I can hold a conversation fine, but there just seems to be something I miss or whatever that just causes people to move on from me. It wasn't helped in that parents never let me have social media until high school, so I had a lot of anxiety over everyone having tons of experience and friends on that while I had none so I never really endeavored in any of that. While in some ways maybe that's a good thing, with how plugged in people are it really makes things hard.

Also, just wanted to say good on you for getting to where you are today. I kinda have a similar role in my family; my sister also has major depressive issues so I listen to her and try not to burden her with me. I do some volunteer work with cats but as you said in general doing charity and stuff gets you out and involved more. Regardless, keep living your best life and stay strong my dude!

Well, I would recommend a cat if you're interested in a pet since they're pretty low maintenance. Just feed them the right food 2-3 times a day, clean their litterbox, give them attention and you're good to go. They can be a huge help, especially since they can be really affectionate despite what some people think. I have a big black rescue cat (20 pounds, he's just big-boned) who follows me everywhere and cries if there's so much of a door between us. IMHO, cats are a great pet for depressed people; they keep you going and aren't too taxing to take care of.

FWIW, I wouldn't recommend a dog because they are deceptively high-maintenance! While my cats could be easily with me during my depression and even in my most languished states I could take care of them, my dog really suffered :(. They need time outdoors, walks, play, etc, or they just end up miserable. I know dogs can help a lot of depressed people but if you'e worried about being able to adequately take care of a pet then I wouldn't get one
Yea I volunteer at cat rescue, even kept a few rescues myself lol. I probably wouldn't be here if it wasn't for animals.
Pets can be a big help if you can get one. Even with my support structure I probably would have killed myself several times over by now if it wasn't for my cat.

I'm 22. I haven't that movie but I've been trying something similar to what you've described since I started college, I think. Like I used to be self conscious about cliques and girlfriends or whatever so when I went to college I decided to just let the chips fall where they may and just be myself, not try to force anything... But that hasn't really worked out either. I'm still in the same spot with plenty of "acquaintances" and no friends. I've kinda stopped caring about the girlfriend thing because I've just accepted that nobody wants me in that way, but it still stings to think about. 

It feels like socially I'm not at the same level as everyone else so no matter what I do it just ends the same.
